segments.original: Michael Curtiz's (1886-1962) Yankee Doodle Dandy (1942) was in tune with the mood of a nation entering World War II, being patriotic, sentimental, aggressive and almost a deification of President Franklin D. Roosevelt, as were its pretentious subject and the songs and choreography of George M. Cohan (James Cagney). The closing of markets in war-ravaged Europe forced Hollywood to seek foreign income in Latin America, which led to a mini boom of Latin American musicals such as Down Argentine Way (1940), starring Carmen Miranda (1909-1955).

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, the great musical stars of the 1930s, reunited for one last, weak film, The Barkleys of Broadway (1949), but Astaire was much more at ease in the company of singer Bing Crosby in films such as Holiday Inn (1942). His standing as the leading name in musicals was being threatened by the younger and obviously more athletic Gene Kelly (1912-1996), who debuted with For Me and My Gal (1942) and was soon creating innovative works such as Anchors Aweigh (1945), in which he dances with the cartoon star MGM's Jerry Mouse, and Cover Girl (1944), in which he dances with his own reflection.

tracks.title: Take Me Out to the Ball Game

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: Anchors Aweigh, about sailors on leave desperate to see a show at the Hollywood Bowl, and the sports-themed Take Me Out to the Ball Game (1949), the last film directed solely by Busby Berkeley (1895-1976), are forerunners of On the Town (1949). Directed by Gene Kelly and Stanley Donen (b. 1924) and inspired by Leonard Bernstein's 1944 Broadway show, the songwriting team of Bernstein, Adolph Green and Betty Comden worked with Roger Edens on several numbers for the film.

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: Cinema has been filming itself since the silent era (Merton of the Movies, 1924). A devastating mix of gossip, glamour, tragedy and a touch of self-promotion makes up the similar What Price Hollywood? (1932) and A Star Is Born (1937, 1954, 1976 and 2018). A later cycle deals with sacred monsters in gothic California mansions, starting with the pessimistic Sunset Boulevard (1950). Specific segments of the film industry are examined in Ed Wood (1994) and Gods and Monsters (1998). But Michael Powell's (1905-1990) Peeping Tom (1960), about a cameraman and killer, and Richard Rush's (b. 1929) The Stunt Man (1980), featuring a Mephistophelean director, suggest that there is something sick about the art of filmmaking.

segments.original: For example, the motto of Kelly's vain movie star is "Dignity, always dignity", inspired by the tumbling of his vaudeville shows early in his career. Interestingly, this became the theme of Minnelli's answer film, the innovative, risqué and divinely creative backstage musical The Band Wagon (1953). segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: The Broadway hit Oklahoma! (1943) was the emblematic musical of its time, but it only reached the screen in 1955. Directed by Fred Zinnemann (1907-1997), its long run encouraged Western musicals off the singing-cowboy trail, but its importance lies in confirming the direct link between Broadway and Hollywood, which kept up a flow of stage-to-screen adaptations throughout the decade, among them Show Boat (1951), Carmen Jones (1954), Guys and Dolls (1955), The King and I (1956), South Pacific (1958) and Porgy and Bess (1959).

segments.original: In 1956, Elvis Presley made his film debut with Love Me Tender (1956). The musicals that followed were built around his sexualized, simple-hearted presence, but his potential was sabotaged by poor career management. Frank Tashlin's (1913-1972) The Girl Can't Help It (1956) was the first great pop musical, with appearances by attractive young artists such as Eddie Cochran (1938-1960), Little Richard and Fats Domino.
